children: NetApp, a data storage company, reported stronger-than-expected earnings and raised its fiscal year guidance on Wednesday, but its stock was falling anyway.

Revenue grew 30% from the prior year to $2.03 billion, topping Wall Street's estimates of $1.84 billion, according to FactSet. The company posted adjusted earnings of $2.58 per share for its fiscal first quarter ended July 31, beating analyst forecasts for $2.12 a share.
Still, NetApp stock declined 8.3% to $165.80 in Thursday's premarket. Shares dropped 1.3% to $180.77 during regular trading hours.
While earnings beat estimates, other numbers in the report may have sent the shares lower.
NetApp's cash from operations dropped by a quarter year over year, and free cash flow declined 35% in that time, while restructuring costs surged to $56 million from $2 million.
In addition, inventory rose from $198 million to $375 million as turnover slowed to less than half the rate reported a year earlier.

The earnings also surpassed NetApp's projections for this quarter. The company expected revenue for the first fiscal quarter to range from $1.75 billion to $1.9 billion, with projected adjusted earnings of $2.05 to $2.15.

NetApp now projects revenue for the fiscal year ending April 30, 2027, to range from $7.98 billion to $8.23 billion with projected adjusted earnings of $9.73 a share to $10.03 a share. That's an increase from previous company profit forecasts of $8.70 a share to $9 a share, with revenue of $7.33 billion to $7.57 billion.
